newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber futures ends up on brisk buying.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber futures ends up on brisk buying.

text.p: Rubber futures finished higher on Tuesday as buying picked up after a slow morning session, largely on fresh orders by some European and Japanese houses, dealers said.
The buying was partly inspired by the higher close of Japanese prices, with the benchmark July contract in Tokyo shooting up 5.7 yen to close at 161.7 yen.

"We ran into some buying by people representing European and Japanese interests who felt prices had become attractive. That helped pushed the market up," a rubber dealer in a foreign trading house said.

Most of the buying was for RSS3 and some RSS1 rubber. The most active months were the June and May RSS3 contracts with some 1,000 and 950 tonnes traded, respectively. About 750 tonnes of the October/December RSS3 contract was also traded.
At around 0945 GMT, April RSS3 was seen at 122.50-124.50 U.S. cents a kg from the previous 122.25 cents.
April RSS1 was seen at 172.50-174.50 Singapore cents (US$1.21-$1.23) a kg from the previous 172.50 cents.
May TSR20 was seen at 169.75-171.75 Singapore cents (US$1.20-$1.21) a kg against 169.75 cents.
